From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Nightly capacity bump for FinLytics POC - latency sweep

Hey Mateo,

We kicked off the latency sweep last night and hit a gap in usable headroom around 23:00 EST. The POC needs one controlled overnight run to validate p95 at target QPS across our real production payloads (session-based inference). Specifically:
- Target window: 2026-11-22 02:00–08:00 UTC (6h)
- Expected sustained QPS: ~650–800 (peak 1,200 for short intervals)
- Payload size: ~1.2k tokens/request on average

Our trial account shows it will exhaust the current allowance within ~3h at those rates. Can Redwood provide a temporary credit top-up or promo allocation to cover a single-night soak (6–12h window)? We'll run the standard test harness and share the telemetry for retention/regression checks.

Also, can you share any recommended config (batching / kv cache hints) that will keep latency stable during the run?

Appreciate a quick yes/no today — we have a tight window.

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Head of Infrastructure
FinLytics

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and the heads-up.

We can provision a one-off promotional allowance to cover the overnight soak. Proposal below:
- 36-hour provisional promo credit: 200,000 tokens (covers the 6h window plus buffer)
- Activation window: please confirm start in UTC; we will enable for the exact 6h slot you provided or a 12h window if you prefer buffer
- Notes: promo is a one-time exception tied to DL-8472 and will be reconciled with the account team post-run.

Quick config suggestions to keep p95 stable:
- Keep batch size small (8–16) for latency-sensitive endpoints; use continuous batching with max latency 50ms
- Enable prefix cache for session lookups, TTL 24h
- Use the rtx-q4f quantized variant if you need cost savings — we can auto-fallback to full precision if you see regressions

I attached a short POC plan template (POC_load_plan.pdf) — if you can upload the start time and endpoint names to that doc I’ll push the promo through. I’ve looped in Vanessa (account lead) and Monica (solutions) for approvals and implementation.

—Mateo
